TABATABAI:11:36-49#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:36-49#7/r1.claim: Noah's son stayed outside the ark, disbelieving his father's warning and trusting a mountain; the wave separated them and drowned the son.

TABATABAI:11:36-49#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:36-49#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:36-49#7/r2.claim: Noah had not known that his son concealed unbelief, unlike his knowledge of his wife; otherwise the son's fate would not have grieved him, since Noah had prayed for the unbelievers' destruction.

TABATABAI:11:42-44/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:42-44/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:42-44/r5.claim: The son had withdrawn to a distant place; Noah's calling rather than simply speaking to him signals that separation, while the diminutive 'my son' conveys compassion.

TABATABAI:11:42-44/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:42-44/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:42-44/r6.claim: Noah says not to be with the unbelievers so his son will not share their punishment as he shared their company; Noah does not yet know his son is inwardly an unbeliever.

TABATABAI:11:42-44/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:42-44/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:42-44/r7.claim: The son expects a mountain to protect him, but Noah says no mountain or other refuge can protect anyone from God's decree of drowning, except those who take refuge in God.

TABATABAI:11:42-44/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:42-44/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:42-44/r8.claim: The wave cuts off their conversation; had it not done so, Noah would have learned his son's unbelief and disowned him.

TABATABAI:11:42-44/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:42-44/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:42-44/r9.claim: The setting's mountainous terrain made it easy for a person to climb one of the local mountains.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The word amr in both verses means punishment as a directive of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The verse presents the final scene of this horrific tragedy.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:42/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:42/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:42/r1.claim: Noah’s fourth son Yam, identified through Ibn Kathir, thought the flood was an ordinary disaster and expected a mountain to save him; Noah’s appeal failed and he drowned with the unbelievers.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:42/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:42/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:42/r2.claim: Views differ on whether the flood covered the whole world or only Noah’s region; the statement that Noah’s offspring alone remained (37:77) seems to support the global view, but no decisive Qur’an or Sunna proof settles its extent, so either is possible.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:42/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:42/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:42/r3.claim: What is certain is that Noah’s people drowned for disobeying him and the believers were saved with Noah.

STUDYQURAN:11:43/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:43/r1.speaker: IK, Z
STUDYQURAN:11:43/r1.claim: One report names Noah’s son who stayed behind Yām.

STUDYQURAN:11:43/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:43/r2.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:11:43/r2.claim: Another reported name for Noah’s son is Kanʿān.

STUDYQURAN:11:43/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:43/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:11:43/r3.claim: Spiritually, the mountain represents the false security, stability, and permanence that deniers of God assign to the world.
